title: DevRev POC Plan — Audyence (HubSpot Replacement)
summary: End-to-end DevRev demo for Audyence, a B2B programmatic audience platform replacing HubSpot. The plan covers the full product hierarchy (platform → capabilities → features → enhancements), representative customer accounts and contacts (rev-users), support tickets tied to engineering issues, a sample incident, and relationship links — demonstrating how DevRev unifies CRM, product, and support in a single surface relevant to Audyence's martech world.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure Pipeline Stages for Audyence Deal Tracking (CRM)
steps: In DevRev, navigate to Settings and find the Pipeline or Funnel configuration section.
Create a new pipeline named 'Audyence New Business' with stages that reflect Audyence's sales motion: Prospecting → Discovery → Demo Delivered → POC Active → Proposal Sent → Closed Won / Closed Lost.
Create a second pipeline named 'Audyence Expansion' for upsell/cross-sell motions with stages: Identified → Scoping → Proposal → Closed.
Assign the Momentum Media Agency and Vertex Demand Partners accounts to opportunities in the appropriate pipeline to demonstrate pipeline-driven CRM replacing HubSpot deals.
Note: pipeline stage configuration is performed in the DevRev UI and is not yet available via the public REST API in v1.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Set Up SLA Policies for Audyence Support Tiers
steps: Navigate to Settings → Support → SLA Policies in the DevRev UI.
Create an 'Enterprise SLA' policy (matching Momentum Media Agency's tier): First Response < 1 hour, Resolution < 4 hours for P1; First Response < 4 hours, Resolution < 24 hours for P2.
Create a 'Growth SLA' policy (matching Vertex Demand Partners' tier): First Response < 4 hours, Resolution < 24 hours for P1.
Assign the Enterprise SLA to the Momentum Media Agency account and Growth SLA to Vertex Demand Partners to demonstrate tier-based support management.
Note: SLA policy creation and assignment must be done in the DevRev UI; it is not available via REST API in v1.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Create Workflow Automations (Snap-ins) for Audyence Use Cases
steps: Explore the DevRev Snap-in marketplace at https://developer.devrev.ai/beta/about/for-developers to find pre-built automations relevant to Audyence.
Configure an automation: When a ticket's severity is set to P1 and it is linked to the DSP Integrations capability, auto-escalate to the on-call engineering lead.
Configure an automation: When an engineering issue linked to a customer ticket transitions to 'Resolved', automatically notify the associated rev-user (customer contact) via email.
Configure a HubSpot migration snap-in (if available) to import existing HubSpot contacts as rev-users and HubSpot companies as accounts, preserving deal history as linked work items.
Note: snap-in configuration and workflow automation require the DevRev UI or snap-in SDK; they cannot be scripted via the basic REST API.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure Custom Fields for Martech / Audyence Context
steps: Navigate to Settings → Custom Fields in the DevRev UI.
Add a custom field 'DSP Platforms' (multi-select: TTD, DV360, Amazon DSP, MediaMath, Xandr) on the Account object to track which DSPs each customer uses.
Add a custom field 'Audience Type' (select: Lookalike, Intent, Retargeting, Contextual) on Ticket and Issue objects to classify work by audience category.
Add a custom field 'ARR' (currency) on the Account object to replicate HubSpot's deal value tracking at the account level.
Add a custom field 'Campaign Go-Live Date' (date) on Ticket objects to prioritize support requests by customer campaign urgency.
Note: custom field creation is performed in the DevRev UI settings and is not available via the public REST API in v1.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Build Saved Views and Dashboards for Audyence Teams
steps: In DevRev, create a saved view named 'Open DSP Integration Tickets' filtered by: type = ticket, applies_to_part = DSP Integrations capability, status = open. Share with the Customer Success team.
Create a saved view named 'Enterprise Customer Issues' filtered by: account tier = enterprise, type = ticket OR issue, status ≠ closed. This replicates the HubSpot 'high-value accounts' view.
Create a product team view: type = issue, capability = Audience Segmentation Engine OR DSP Integrations, sprint = current — for the engineering standup.
Create an executive dashboard showing: open P1/P2 tickets by account tier, active incidents, and enhancement delivery rate for the current quarter.
Note: saved views and custom dashboards are configured in the DevRev UI and are not available via REST API in v1.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Sprint / Iteration Board Setup for Audyence Engineering Demo
steps: Open DevRev and navigate to your sprint or curated iteration view.
Create a sprint named 'Audyence Sprint 1 — DSP Stability' and assign the TTD latency issue (demo-iss-ttd-latency) and overlap bug issue (demo-iss-overlap-bug) to it.
Create a second sprint 'Audyence Sprint 2 — Onboarding Scale' and assign the CSV limit issue (demo-iss-csv-limit).
Walk the demo audience through the board to show how engineering priorities are directly traceable to customer tickets from Momentum Media and Vertex — the key story vs HubSpot + Jira.
Note: automated sprint discovery in the CLI aggregates sprint metadata from works.list responses and may miss empty sprints.

steps.title: Create product: Audyence Platform
steps.rationale: Establishes the top-level product node in DevRev's part hierarchy, representing Audyence's core B2B programmatic audience platform. This is the anchor for all capabilities, features, and work items in the demo.

body.name: Audyence Platform
body.description: B2B programmatic audience targeting platform enabling media buyers and sellers to activate first- and third-party audience data across DSPs.

steps.title: Create capability: Audience Segmentation Engine
steps.rationale: Core differentiating capability for Audyence — building and activating B2B audience segments. Demonstrating this as a tracked capability shows engineering and product alignment within DevRev.

steps.title: Create capability: DSP Integrations
steps.rationale: Audyence distributes audiences across demand-side platforms (DSPs). Tracking this as a distinct capability allows the team to link customer support issues directly to integration health, replacing scattered HubSpot notes.

steps.title: Create capability: Data Marketplace & Onboarding
steps.rationale: Customer onboarding and data provider marketplace are key GTM motions for Audyence. Representing this capability lets CS and engineering collaborate on onboarding issues without leaving DevRev.

steps.title: Create capability: Reporting & Analytics
steps.rationale: Media buyers and brand marketers expect detailed campaign and audience performance reporting. Surfacing this as a capability demonstrates DevRev's ability to tie feature requests from customers directly to roadmap items.

steps.title: Create feature: Lookalike Audience Builder
steps.rationale: A flagship feature for Audyence — generating lookalike segments from seed audiences. Tracking it as a feature under Segmentation Engine lets the team link inbound customer asks (tickets) directly to the feature roadmap.

steps.title: Create feature: Intent Data Activation
steps.rationale: B2B intent data is central to Audyence's value prop. Representing this as a tracked feature enables product managers to see support signals and enhancement requests in one place, replacing HubSpot deal notes.

steps.title: Create feature: Trade Desk (TTD) Connector
steps.rationale: The Trade Desk is a primary DSP partner for Audyence. Modeling the connector as a feature lets support, CS, and engineering triage integration issues with full product context — a key HubSpot gap.

steps.title: Create feature: Customer Onboarding Workflow
steps.rationale: Audyence onboards agencies and brand marketers who need guided setup. Tracking onboarding as a feature surfaces friction points reported by rev-users (customers) directly to product engineering.

steps.title: Create feature: Campaign Performance Dashboard
steps.rationale: Media buyer personas expect real-time campaign reporting. Tracking this feature enables the team to close the loop between customer-reported dashboard bugs (tickets) and the engineering backlog.

steps.title: Create enhancement: Saved Segment Templates
steps.rationale: A concrete, customer-requested enhancement under the Lookalike Audience Builder. Demonstrates how DevRev tracks granular product improvements with full traceability from customer request to shipped enhancement.

steps.title: Create enhancement: CSV Audience Upload
steps.rationale: A frequent onboarding ask from new Audyence customers who want to seed audiences from their own CRM data. Logging this enhancement links the customer voice (rev-users) to the product roadmap.

steps.title: Create account: Momentum Media Agency
steps.rationale: Representative agency customer for Audyence — a media buying shop activating B2B audiences for clients. Creating this account in DevRev replaces the HubSpot company record and links support, product, and revenue signals.

body.description: Full-service B2B media agency using Audyence for programmatic audience activation across DSPs.

steps.title: Create account: Vertex Demand Partners
steps.rationale: Representative brand marketer / demand-side account. Showing multiple account types in the demo illustrates DevRev's CRM breadth to replace HubSpot's contact and company management.

body.description: B2B brand marketing team leveraging Audyence intent data for account-based advertising campaigns.

steps.title: Create rev-user: Jamie Caldwell (Momentum Media Agency)
steps.rationale: Customer contact at the agency account — maps directly to a HubSpot contact record. Rev-users in DevRev are first-class citizens linked to accounts, tickets, and revenue, unifying what HubSpot kept siloed from engineering.

steps.title: Create rev-user: Priya Nair (Vertex Demand Partners)
steps.rationale: Customer contact at the brand marketer account. Including multiple rev-users demonstrates DevRev's multi-contact account model, a key capability Audyence needs to replace HubSpot's contact management.

steps.title: Create ticket: TTD connector sync delay — Momentum Media
steps.rationale: Real-world support scenario: an agency customer reports audience segments aren't syncing to The Trade Desk on time. Logging this as a ticket linked to a rev-user and product part shows how DevRev connects customer pain to engineering — replacing HubSpot support tickets that had no product traceability.

body.title: TTD connector sync delay — audiences not activating within SLA
body.body: Jamie Caldwell at Momentum Media reports that audience segments uploaded on Monday are not visible in TTD until 6+ hours later, missing campaign launch windows.

steps.title: Create ticket: CSV upload fails for large seed files — Vertex
steps.rationale: Priya at Vertex Demand Partners hits an error uploading a 50k-row CSV to seed a lookalike audience. This ticket demonstrates the rev-user → ticket → feature traceability that replaces fragmented HubSpot support email threads.

body.title: CSV audience upload fails for files over 10k rows
body.body: Priya Nair (Vertex Demand Partners) reports a 500 error when uploading CSV seed files larger than 10,000 rows. Smaller files succeed. Blocking onboarding of their key accounts list.

steps.title: Create ticket: Dashboard not rendering segment overlap report
steps.rationale: A reporting bug that a media buyer persona would encounter. Linking this ticket to the Campaign Performance Dashboard feature closes the loop between the customer experience and the product team's backlog — impossible in HubSpot.

body.title: Segment overlap report renders blank on Campaign Performance Dashboard
body.body: Multiple customers report the segment overlap visualization is blank after the v2.4 dashboard release. Workaround: export raw CSV. Affects reporting workflows for all active campaigns.

steps.title: Create issue: Fix TTD audience sync pipeline latency
steps.rationale: Engineering issue spawned by the Momentum Media support ticket. This is the core DevRev 'aha moment' vs HubSpot — the same platform that logged the customer complaint now tracks the fix, with full bidirectional traceability.

body.title: Reduce TTD audience sync pipeline latency from ~6h to <30min
body.body: Root cause: batch job runs every 6 hours. Migrate to event-driven sync triggered on segment publish. Affects enterprise SLA commitments.

steps.title: Create issue: Increase CSV upload limit to 500k rows
steps.rationale: Engineering issue addressing Vertex's onboarding blocker. Demonstrates that a customer-reported ticket can spawn a product enhancement issue, keeping CS and engineering in sync without context-switching out of DevRev.

body.title: Increase CSV audience upload file size limit from 10k to 500k rows
body.body: Current 10k row hard limit is blocking enterprise onboarding. Requires chunked upload implementation and async processing queue. Linked to CSV Audience Upload enhancement.

steps.title: Create issue: Fix segment overlap visualization rendering bug
steps.rationale: Engineering issue tied to the dashboard bug ticket and the v2.4 regression. Illustrates how DevRev's unified platform surfaces the customer impact of engineering regressions without needing a separate HubSpot-to-Jira hand-off.

body.title: Fix segment overlap chart rendering regression introduced in v2.4
body.body: Null pointer exception in D3 chart component when overlap data set is empty. Introduced in v2.4 dashboard refactor. High customer visibility.

steps.title: Create incident: DSP Sync Outage — all connectors
steps.rationale: A production incident scenario relevant to Audyence's business: all DSP audience syncs are failing. DevRev's incident management linked to product parts and customer tickets demonstrates a single pane of glass that HubSpot could never provide for an engineering-heavy martech company.

body.title: P1 Incident: DSP audience sync service down — all connectors affected
body.body: Audience sync microservice is returning 503s across all DSP connectors (TTD, DV360, Amazon DSP). Segments are not activating. Customer campaigns are at risk. Initiated runbook DSP-INC-001.

steps.title: Link: TTD sync ticket → TTD latency engineering issue
steps.rationale: Connects Momentum Media's support ticket directly to the engineering fix, giving CS reps real-time visibility into resolution progress — replacing the manual HubSpot-to-Jira status update loop.

steps.title: Link: CSV upload ticket → CSV limit engineering issue
steps.rationale: Traces Vertex Demand Partners' onboarding blocker ticket to the engineering backlog item. Demonstrates DevRev's customer-to-code traceability that is the key differentiator vs HubSpot for a product-led company like Audyence.

steps.title: Link: Dashboard bug ticket → overlap rendering issue
steps.rationale: Connects the customer-visible dashboard bug report to the engineering regression fix, enabling the support team to update customers automatically as the issue progresses through the sprint.

steps.title: Link: DSP outage incident → TTD sync ticket
steps.rationale: Associates the active P1 incident with the pre-existing customer support ticket about TTD latency, showing that DevRev can surface at-risk accounts during an incident — a powerful CRM + ops story vs HubSpot.

steps.title: Link: CSV limit issue → CSV Upload enhancement
steps.rationale: Connects the active engineering fix to the product enhancement it will ship as, demonstrating end-to-end roadmap visibility from customer request (Priya's ticket) to enhancement to shipped feature.

steps.title: Link: Saved Segment Templates enhancement → Lookalike Audience Builder feature
steps.rationale: Explicitly surfaces the enhancement-to-feature relationship in the graph so product managers can walk stakeholders through the roadmap hierarchy during the demo, replacing static HubSpot deal notes with live product context.
